# Remove-ZbxRegExp

## SYNOPSIS

Removes global regular expressions.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxRegExp [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixRegExp>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A global regular expression is a named set of expressions that log items, low-level discovery filters and other fields refer to as @name. The Remove-ZbxRegExp cmdlet deletes the global regular expressions given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with regexp.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a global regular expression

```powershell
Remove-ZbxRegExp -InputObject 'Application errors' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the global regular expression Application errors. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the global regular expressions a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxRegExp -Name 'Application*' | Remove-ZbxRegExp -WhatIf
```

Lists the global regular expressions whose names start with Application that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
